user.description: Where should the Prusa Connect server run?

menu_options.embedded: Inside Home Assistant (install and run it here)

embedded.title: Run Prusa Connect inside Home Assistant
embedded.description: Home Assistant downloads the newest Prusa Connect release, checks its signature and runs it. Printers and your browser connect to it at the address and port below.

data.host: Address of the Home Assistant device

data_description.port: A port no other service on this machine uses.
data_description.host: Printers and your browser connect to the server at this address. Use the IP address of the device itself. A reverse proxy in front of Home Assistant does not forward this port, so its address will not work here.

external.title: Connect to Prusa Connect
external.description: Enter the address of your Prusa Connect server, for example https://192.168.1.10:8080.

data_description.url: The origin the Prusa Connect web app opens on, with its port.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Discovered Prusa Connect
zeroconf_confirm.description: Do you want to set up {name} at {url}?

certificate.title: Trust this certificate?
certificate.description:
The server at {url} presents a certificate that this system does not trust, which is normal for a server that made its own certificate authority. Compare this SHA-256 fingerprint with the one Prusa Connect shows, and submit only if they match:

`{fingerprint}`

Home Assistant then trusts exactly this certificate and no other.

auth.title: Sign in to Prusa Connect
auth.description: How should Home Assistant get access to {url}?

menu_options.pair: Pair with a code (approve it in Prusa Connect)

token.title: API token
token.description: In Prusa Connect at {url}, open Settings, then API credentials (/settings/tokens), and create a token for Home Assistant. Paste it here. A token can be valid for at most 365 days; you will be asked for a new one when it expires.

data_description.token: A bearer token starting with pcl_.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The token for {url} is no longer accepted.

reauth_token.title: New API token
reauth_token.description: Create a new token in Prusa Connect at {url} and paste it here.

progress.wait_for_approval: Open {url} and sign in to Prusa Connect. Check that the code is **{code}**, then approve Home Assistant. This window continues on its own once you approve.
progress.install: Downloading Prusa Connect and checking its signature, then starting it…
progress.first_run:
Open {url} and finish Prusa Connect's first-run wizard. When it asks for the setup code, enter:

**{code}**

Create your administrator there. This window continues on its own when the wizard is done.

data.sidebar: Show the web app in the sidebar

data_description.cameras: Create a camera entity for every camera declared in Prusa Connect.
data_description.update_throttle: Readings arrive several times a second; they are written to Home Assistant at most this often.
data_description.sidebar: A sidebar item opens Prusa Connect inside Home Assistant. You sign in to Prusa Connect there.
data_description.panel_url: The address your browser opens Prusa Connect at, when it differs from the one Home Assistant uses. A Home Assistant served over https needs an https address here.
data_description.prerelease: The update entity offers pre-releases of the server too, not only stable ones.
